items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1960-01-28
items.q: On a Monday night, it was our pay night, and he'd come up to Emble Up and give Russell, give a little Russell Emble Up to pay us off, and with a big smile on his face.

ctx.x: What kind of a place was it?

All this place happened to be down in the basement, you know? It was down in the basement. I had a full show there. It was a good show. Casper Holstein, which was the proprietor, he was a very nice man. You didn't have to worry about your money. I mean, whether he did business or not, he always had a smile on his face. You see, if they wouldn't have many people all the week, he never tormented the band, say to the band, and, man, he's not playing. I mean, what's happening to the band, and what's this and what's…
He did a lot of arrangements, you know.

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: I'm talking about that guy used to be with Louis Ruffalo.

ctx.x: Yeah, 39. Didn't use no amplifier. No. You know the boy in the band, Lee Blatt, didn't use it, no. Will Johnson didn't use it either. Well, Will Johnson played more of the banjo than he did the guitar, because he had a small guitar. I think it was a four-string guitar, I think he had. You recall that?
I never saw Bill Johnson in my life. You never saw Bill Johnson? I'm talking about that guy used to be with Louis Ruffalo. I never saw him.
